name: Serum Creatinine
description: Serum creatinine measuring endogenous product of muscle catabolism cleared almost entirely by glomerular filtration
reportDescription: Measures serum creatinine concentration to assess glomerular filtration function.
interpretationGuidance: Elevated creatinine levels indicate impaired glomerular filtration or acute/chronic renal dysfunction.

name: Blood Urea
description: Blood urea measuring major end product of protein nitrogen metabolism synthesized by liver and cleared by renal excretion
reportDescription: Measures blood urea level as a marker of protein metabolism and renal excretory capacity.
interpretationGuidance: Elevated blood urea indicates azotemia, dehydration, gastrointestinal bleeding, or impaired renal perfusion and excretion.

name: Sodium
description: Major extracellular cation regulating osmotic pressure, fluid distribution, and neuromuscular function
interpretationGuidance: Hyponatremia or hypernatremia indicates disturbances in water balance, renal tubular function, or neuroendocrine regulation.

name: Potassium
description: Major intracellular cation essential for cellular membrane potential, cardiac rhythmicity, and neuromuscular excitability
interpretationGuidance: Hyperkalemia or hypokalemia carries serious risk of cardiac arrhythmias and neuromuscular dysfunction.

name: Chloride
description: Major extracellular anion maintaining electrical neutrality, acid-base equilibrium, and osmotic balance
interpretationGuidance: Hypochloremia or hyperchloremia generally accompanies sodium abnormalities and acid-base disturbances.

name: Total Calcium
description: Total serum calcium including ionized, protein-bound, and complexed fractions evaluating mineral homeostasis
reportDescription: Measures total circulating calcium in serum.
interpretationGuidance: Hypocalcemia or hypercalcemia reflects parathyroid, renal, skeletal, or protein-binding alterations.
